message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Standard atomic weight** | 1.008 u (average of isotopes) |
| **Isotopes** | ¹H (protium, 99.98 %), ²H (deuterium, 0.02 %), ³H (tritium, trace) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ (negative, so it releases energy when gaining an electron) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.9 °C (20.3 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.2 °C (14.0 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.00008988 g cm⁻³) |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| **Reactivity** | Extremely reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many non‑metals; reacts violently with oxygen at high temperatures. |
| **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds (H₂), ionic bonds (as H⁺ or H⁻), and participates in hydrogen bonding (in water, alcohols, etc.). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series in UV/visible/IR; prominent 21‑cm line from hyperfine transition in interstellar medium. |
| **Physical state** | Gas at room temperature; liquid under high pressure; solid at very low temperatures. |
| **Solubility in water** | ~0.0016 g g⁻¹ at 25 °C (very low). |
| **Flammability** | Highly flammable; explosive mixture with air (4–75 % H₂). |
| **Acid–base behavior** | Acts as a weak acid (forming H₃O⁺) and a weak base (forming H₂O). |
| **Oxidation states** | +1 (as H⁺), –1 (as H⁻), 0 (as H₂). |
| **Common compounds** | H₂O, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, HF, etc. |
| **Industrial uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), ammonia synthesis (Haber process), petroleum refining, metal processing, semiconductor manufacturing. |
| **Environmental role** | Major component of the universe (~75 % by mass); key in stellar nucleosynthesis and interstellar chemistry. |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element** – lowest density, lowest boiling/melting points.
- **Highly reactive** – forms a wide variety of compounds; essential in both organic and inorganic chemistry.
- **Versatile bonding** – participates in covalent, ionic, and hydrogen bonds.
- **Key industrial & energy player** – central to fuel cells, ammonia production, and many manufacturing processes.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
